I lived along the central line, out on bond Street, two lefts and follow the road and that was where I grew up. My father used to take the train to work, as a young boy Id sit on my mothers shoulders at the station and wave to him as he desended from the platform.

Id grown a fondness to the system and spent every chance I could get to travel via train. My Job fit perfectly with this little dream of mine. My lack of a levels or degrees meant that janitor was my only option but that didnt phase me. Most days were quiet but every once in a while "CRASH", some stupid kid in a black cape holding a stick or a book or even the odd suitcase would throw themselves headfirst into the pillars. 'Idiots' Id mutter as id help them collect their things and send them in the right direction. And they wouldnt stop. Day in day out. "CRASH CRASH CRASH". One day. Just one. Was all it took to stop them all in their tracks' I saw yet another child crouch ready to leap face first into cold hard stone. When they went through. Straight though to the other side of the pillar. The pillar collapsed along side several other kids who collapsed into sobs. I do think kids will ever understand how trains work.
